title: QUIC: Don't warn on secrets not being available
description: Don't give a warning about secrets not being available for QUIC packets, we don't do this for TLS and it's not really an error just expected behavior.

notes.body:
Personally I find it useful to have some element added to the tree that is easy to filter on to indicate that decrypted succeeded or failed, and find it frustrating that not all protocols have it.

I could certainly see an argument for a lower level for the missing keys case (Info) compared to others. Note that there are plenty of expert infos that do not indicate errors but quite common if notable behaviors.
See, for example, issue #13297, where @Lekensteyn suggested that having no key log file configured is something that perhaps should be an expert info at some severity (even though not an error.)

Yeah, I can understand the desire to want to know when something did/didn't decrypt so as to be able to filter on that. My initial annoyance was that it was flagging on every connection it saw when no key log is loaded to the point I started ignoring the warning which made it feel kinda useless/spammy. When I noticed that it didn't do that for TLS packets I figured it would be a good opportunity to bring them in line.

I could change this patch to only warn on failure if a key log is currently loaded, or I could lower the severity as you suggested, or maybe both. Do you have a preference to any of those in particular?

I personally still lean towards at least making it show nothing when a key log is not loaded to try to reduce superfluous messages to people but I'm open to input.
+1 about check the key log file and ok for change the level (but may need to create a new expert field)

> I personally still lean towards at least making it show nothing when a key log is not loaded

+1

> I personally still lean towards at least making it show nothing when a key log is not loaded

I understand the POV, but we get a lot of questions and issues filed from users who have trouble with decryption, and sometimes it's that they forgot to configure their keylog file, or accidentally erased it by configuring their keylog file as the debug log file.

A specific, if lower priority, expert info of "this isn't being decrypted because you haven't configured a key log file" might be useful for many new users.

> A specific, if lower priority, expert info of "this isn't being decrypted because you haven't configured a key log file" might be useful for many new users.

I am fine with that also. But I think that we should have the same behavior for QUIC and TLS (and any other protocols using decryption keys)
